statement: While a video plays, the battery level $B$ of a phone, as a percent of a full charge, decreases linearly with time. The table shows $B$ at $t$ minutes after the video starts. $$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c} t & 10 & 25 & 40 \\ \hline B & 86 & 74 & 62 \end{array}$$ According to this relationship, how many minutes after the video starts will the battery level be $30$ percent?

choices.misconception: I treated the first column as the start, so I divided the drop from 86 to 30 by 0.8 and got 70, forgetting that 10 minutes had already passed by then.
I assumed the battery was at 100 percent when the video started, so I divided the 70-point drop by 0.8 and got 87.5.
I found when the battery reaches 0 percent, $94 \div 0.8$, instead of when it reaches 30 percent.

hints: How much does the battery level drop per minute?
Find the slope from two columns of the table, then work back to the level at $t = 0$ and write $B$ as a linear function of $t$.
The slope is $\frac{74 - 86}{25 - 10} = -0.8$, so at $t = 0$ the level was $86 + 8 = 94$. Solve $94 - 0.8t = 30$.

solutions.reliable: The slope is $\frac{74 - 86}{25 - 10} = \frac{-12}{15} = -0.8$ percent per minute. Going back $10$ minutes from $(10, 86)$, the level at $t = 0$ was $86 + 0.8(10) = 94$, so $B = 94 - 0.8t$. Setting $B = 30$: $0.8t = 64$ and $t = 80$. Check with the last column: $94 - 0.8(40) = 62$.
solutions.elegant: From $t = 40$, the level must fall another $62 - 30 = 32$ points at $0.8$ points per minute, which takes $40$ more minutes, so $t = 40 + 40 = 80$.
